news.label: OpenAI raises $11B at $1.25T valuation
points: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion.
The funding values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.
The round is not closed yet and could total about $20 billion.
details: Bloomberg reported the funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
The round is expected to close in the coming weeks.
In late September, Bloomberg reported OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion.

news.label: Midterms may bring tougher AI scrutiny
points: Democrats won historic victories in this week's U.S. midterms.
Voters decided on 41 data center-related ballot measures.
In all but one, the majority voted for more restrictions.
details: Newly elected Democratic governors and congressmembers likely support additional regulation.
Data centers were a major talking point even when not directly on the ballot.
TechCrunch's Equity podcast discussed what the election means for the tech industry.

news.label: Meta Muse adds custom spaces
points: Meta now lets users build app-like experiences within Muse.
You can create things like a shopping hub or music tracker.
details: You create a space by describing it to the AI assistant.
Connecting outside apps lets Muse pull information and update your space in the background.
Meta is rolling out spaces to all Muse users.

news.label: Embedded 3D printing with liquids
points: A broken Prusa printer was turned into an embedded 3D printing setup.
The hot-end was replaced with a syringe system.
The method prints materials into a supportive medium.
details: The project used an open source Allstruder syringe pump and a Caribou Duet 3 motherboard.
A test print used cream cheese as the printing material.
A final print used silicone, specifically Sylgard 184, with hair gel as the support medium.

news.label: Alpine Linux on a Kindle Paperwhite 3
points: A distro brings Alpine Linux to the Kindle Paperwhite 3.
The Kindle must be jailbroken and uses an old Amazon kernel.
It includes games, a browser, an ePub reader, and a local chatbot.
details: The chatbot runs SmolLM2 over llama.cpp on the Kindle's own processor.
It runs at 1.7 words per second, but everything stays on the device.
It is easy to return the Kindle to stock.
